description: For adults in transition who can name few people to ask about their goal, repeated structured contact with the same peers, outreach by staff or mentors, and brokered introductions with a follow-up step are expected to yield usable new ties, less isolation and, more slowly, persistence and access to opportunity, though no claim in the wiki tests this against leaving networking to the learner.
title: Expanding Social Networks

description: For learners building applied, professional or interpersonal capability, an experience followed by structured reflection and a further attempt with feedback is expected to improve performance and transfer, while unguided experience for novices learns less than guided instruction.
title: Experiential Learning

description: For adult novices with a device, especially older or low-confidence adults, demonstrating one short routine at a time on their own device, having them do it at once with help that responds to each attempt, and withdrawing that help as they succeed is expected to produce more accurate unaided use of those routines than exploration or explanation alone, though no claim in the wiki tests this for computer basics.
title: Explicit Instruction: Computer Basics

description: For a novice searcher who types whole questions and stops at the first results, explicit modelling of a routine for turning a question into terms, building and revising queries and checking results, practised on real inquiry questions with feedback on the queries, is expected to find more relevant sources with less abandonment than unguided exploration, though no claim in the wiki tests search instruction directly.
title: Explicit Instruction: Internet Search

description: For a learner who can compute but not yet choose a method for word or non-routine problems, explicitly modelling when and why a strategy fits, comparing methods side by side and guiding justified choice are expected to build flexible, accurate problem solving, though no claim in the wiki tests strategy instruction against its absence.
title: Explicit Instruction: Math Strategies

description: For a learner who reads print adequately but navigates linked online texts without a goal, explicit modelled instruction in a few online reading moves (goal and questions before opening links, choosing links against the goal, a running record of pages, returning from drift, combining pages), practised on curated then open sets of pages with prompts that fade, is expected to improve comprehension and integration across pages; no claim tests this, and the nearest evidence is print strategy instruction and computer-based metacognitive prompts.
title: Explicit Instruction: Online Reading Strategies

description: For a learner whose comprehension or use of language is limited by particular unknown words, explicitly teaching a small selected set and then arranging repeated encounters and use across contexts is expected to improve knowledge of those words and comprehension of texts that use them more than exposure alone, which claims test for school-age and second-language learners, but not for general comprehension, dose or schedule.
title: Explicit Instruction: Vocabulary

description: For learners exploring how a system behaves, a computer tool that returns the result of each idea in seconds is expected to let them test more hypotheses with less frustration and spend the saved time interpreting, improving conceptual understanding and inquiry skill when the exploration is guided; no claim in the wiki tests the speed of the cycle itself, though guidance during inquiry is supported.
title: Use computer tools that let students explore hypotheses and solutions faster so they can test many ideas without frustration
